title: A Strong-Field Turn-Off for the Quadrature MOND Kernel: Planetary Safety, a Finite Vacuum Term, and the Offset Reading
description: Version 1.0 (AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed). The quadrature law g^2 = g_N^2 + a0 g_N (nu = sqrt(1 + 1/y), Milgrom 1999 eq 9) has a slow strong-field tail, nu - 1 ~ 1/(2y): held to all accelerations it gives a constant a0/2 anomaly in the Solar System, 1279 times the Earth-Mars ephemeris bound, and it makes the vacuum term of the theory's field Lagrangian (QUMOND, bimetric MOND) diverge. We replace the tail by nu_fix = 1 + (sqrt(1 + 1/y) - 1)/(1 + (y/y_t)^2). On SPARC it is indistinguishable from the exact law for y_t >= 100 (|Delta chi2| <= 1.06); a direct fit bounds y_t only from below; every planet passes for y_t <= 7.7e5; the vacuum term becomes finite, Lambda/a0^2 ~ (pi/4) y_t. Under the offset reading (the a0 sector's vacuum energy is the dark energy, an input) y_t = 128.9 on the kappa = 1/2 footing and 94-103 for measured a0. The value is shape-dependent and does not derive kappa = 1/2, which stays fitted.
